source_snapshot.procedure: In root Profile settings, save Browser offset (Taipei UTC+8) and/or Default UTC, then check the Overview BMC time; source also requests log clearing.
source_snapshot.criteria: Preference changes successfully and BMC time displays correctly.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL browser automation; only says read/change/revert the preference and return before/after setting, without defining time transformation or verifying Overview.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION; per-user display scope, trusted UTC reference, browser offset semantics, underlying-clock isolation and restoration are required.

historical_reviews.deepseek: Its reversible-state warning is correct, but setting readback alone does not prove the rendered Overview time or distinguish display preference from clock mutation.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Reclassification and display-versus-clock boundary are accepted; protected browser session and two-option transformation evidence are retained.
historical_reviews.history: Exact-code searches found no duplicate variant or completed record; system timezone/NTP tests cannot replace this per-user Web display check.
historical_reviews.v3_1: Browser offset is derived from the client environment, while Default UTC is a rendering policy; the underlying BMC epoch must remain invariant across both observations.

original_test_intent: With explicit approval, switch the target BMC Web user's timezone display preference between the specified Browser offset UTC+8 and Default UTC choices, verify Overview renders the same underlying instant correctly, then restore the original preference.
original_method: Bind one BMC, user and browser locale; capture original preference, trusted UTC time and BMC clock source; save one approved preference at a time, revisit Overview and compare rendered time with the expected offset transformation; prove the BMC clock/NTP state did not change and restore the original user preference.
manual_activity: The owner confirms per-user/global scope and expected Browser-offset/UTC transformations; an operator approves the preference writes and verifies the rendered Overview time while automation may capture protected before/after evidence.
required_inputs: Exact SUT/BMC and Web user identity
Browser locale, timezone and actual UTC offset
Expected Browser offset UTC+8 and Default UTC rendering rules
Trusted UTC reference and acceptable display tolerance
Protected browser automation or documented preference API
Restoration path and redacted evidence storage
safety_requirements: Change only the display preference, never BMC clock, RTC, NTP or host timezone
Verify the target user and session before save
Do not expose credentials, cookies or tokens
Use a trusted time reference rather than visual plausibility
Stop on unexpected clock jump, global scope, wrong user or failed save
Do not clear BMC audit, SEL or time evidence
agent_execution_scope: Capture BMC/user/browser identity and original preference
Record trusted UTC and read-only underlying clock evidence
Apply only explicitly approved preference changes through the supported path
Capture Overview after each save and calculate the expected rendering
Restore and report evidence without verdict
engineer_actions: Define browser-offset and UTC mapping plus tolerance
Approve user/scope and each reversible change
Verify the display and original-state restoration
Resolve clock/session anomalies and own PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Read/change/revert is directionally useful, but its evidence omits the required Overview time and does not prove the underlying BMC clock stayed unchanged.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: With approval, save Browser offset UTC+8 and Default UTC one at a time for the verified user, compare Overview to the trusted UTC transformation, confirm the underlying clock is unchanged, then restore the original preference.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Named Web path, two display options and 5/5-minute estimates remain; no BMC clock/NTP mutation or log clearing is added.

modernized_recommendation.status: APPROVAL-GATED PER-USER TIME DISPLAY TRANSFORMATION CHECK
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: For each preference, record browser offset, trusted UTC instant, expected rendered timestamp, observed Overview timestamp, delta/tolerance, save/readback status and invariant underlying clock evidence.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds an objective clock transformation oracle and separates per-user rendering from BMC time configuration.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Preference readback alone covers persistence, not correct Overview rendering; clock equality alone cannot prove the selected presentation rule.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Browser offset may change with client timezone or DST and the setting may be global on some firmware, so scope and environment must be captured.

project_override_considerations: If firmware treats the control as global, impact approval must cover other users and evidence must show restoration. Taipei UTC+8 has no DST, but Browser offset still depends on the actual client configuration rather than the label alone.
expected_evidence: Redacted BMC/user/browser identity, original preference and scope
Trusted UTC reference, browser offset and tolerance
Protected Profile setting before/save/readback captures for both options
Overview expected-versus-observed timestamps for Browser offset and Default UTC
Underlying BMC clock/NTP no-mutation proof, audit events and restored original preference
Engineer-owned PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Title and Procedure clearly target a Web display preference; Criteria's `BMC timezone` wording is shorthand for that saved presentation state because it immediately requires correct displayed time, not an alternate clock-setting command.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The check is executable with normal owner inputs: user/scope, browser offset mapping, trusted time reference, protected Web/API access and restore policy.

review_improvement: Adds the missing time transformation oracle and proves that changing presentation does not mutate the BMC clock, while requiring restoration of the exact user's original setting.
independent_technical_reasoning: Correct timezone display means two representations map to one invariant instant. Capturing a trusted UTC instant and the browser's real offset allows both views to be reconciled; without that invariant, a clock mutation could falsely appear to make each displayed string correct.
